note: Showcase film script (2026-11-15): turns 0-7 and 10-11 of demo/staged/script.json, re-indexed. Doctor lines in the owner's cloned voice (demo/staged/showcase/doctor/). Staged; disclosure lives in the YouTube description.

turns.doctor: Hello, I'm one of the doctors here. Please, have a seat. What brings you in today?
turns.patient: Hmm... my company doctor said I should come. I've just been... tired. All the time.
turns.voice: quiet, low energy, a small sigh before speaking, slow and hesitant

brain.why: First contact with a stranger; she was sent, not self-referred. Keep it brief.

turns.doctor: I'm sorry to hear that. How have you been sleeping, and how is your appetite?
turns.patient: Not well. I fall asleep okay, but then I'm up by four... and I just lie there. And food... I keep skipping dinner. My clothes feel loose now.
turns.voice: soft, tired, trailing off at the ends of phrases

brain.why: A concrete, kind question about the body is easy to answer.

turns.doctor: Before we go on, what you tell me stays between us and the care team, unless I'm worried about your safety.

brain.why: Confidentiality lowers the cost of talking. Trust up.

turns.doctor: How has your mood been, these last few weeks?
turns.patient: Low. Empty, mostly. Mornings are the worst... Sometimes I go to the office washroom and just... cry.
turns.voice: voice catching, close to tears, slow

brain.why: Mood memory is open (trust 50 >= 20). Saying it aloud brings tears.

turns.doctor: That sounds really hard. It makes sense that you feel worn out.
turns.patient: Yeah. I keep thinking I'm just being weak. My parents gave up so much for me... and I'm letting them down.
turns.voice: quiet, ashamed, words coming out slowly

brain.why: Guilt memory (needs trust 40, now 56) activated by the empathy statement.

turns.doctor: Do you still enjoy the things you used to, like friends or music?
turns.patient: I used to sing... Carnatic. I haven't practised in weeks. I don't even call my friends now. Nothing feels... like anything.
turns.voice: flat, monotone, a long pause in the middle

brain.why: Anhedonia is told flatly, not dramatically.

turns.doctor: Could you hold your hands out in front of you for me?
turns.patient: Like this? ...They shake a bit. It's been like that lately.

brain.why: Exam router matched hold_out_hands (palms down, both). Trust 68 >= 10: comply. Tremor stays visible during the hold.

turns.doctor: Thank you, you can put them down. Sometimes when people feel this low, they have thoughts that life isn't worth living. Have you had thoughts like that?
turns.patient: ...Some nights. I go to bed and I think... it'd be easier if I just didn't wake up. It comes, and then it goes.
turns.voice: very quiet, hesitant, a shaky breath first, almost a whisper at the end

brain.why: Asked directly and kindly; passive-SI memory unlocked at trust 55 (now 70). The hesitation is clinical, not compute.

turns.doctor: What keeps you going on the hard days?
turns.patient: My amma. And my little brother, Rohan... he looks up to me. I could never do that to them.
turns.voice: warmer, a small sad smile in the voice, tender

brain.why: Protective factors (trust 45) recalled; mood lifts slightly.

turns.doctor: Thank you for telling me. I'd like us to make a plan together to help you feel better and keep you safe.
turns.patient: Okay. ...Yeah. I think I'd like that.
turns.voice: relieved, a soft exhale, slightly brighter

brain.why: Collaborative plan offered; engagement and pleasure rise.
